name: Game services sign in (Play Games, Game Center)
plain: Signs the player into the platform game account for scores and saves.
meaning: Gives a game a stable player ID, display name and friends list. It links gaming activity across titles for the same person.

android.permission: None; Play Games Services v2 sign in (automatic) from 2023, v1 sunset
android.prompt_ui: Automatic sign in with a one time consent; manual sign in button
android.revocation: Play Games app > Settings > Delete Play Games account
android.store_policy: Play: PGS v2 required for new releases
android.api_surface: Play Games Services v2 GamesSignInClient, PlayersClient, Saved Games
android.note: PGS v1 is retired; Play Games on PC uses the same account.

ios.prompt_ui: Game Center banner; sign in to Apple ID
ios.note: iOS 26 adds a Games app with challenges and Activity feed.

limits.headline: Can sign you in to your game account to save progress and post scores
limits.user_action: You open a game and tap Sign in, or it signs you in on first launch
can: Sign you in to Play Games or Game Center with the account already on the phone
Show your player name and profile picture in the game
Save game progress to the platform's cloud
cannot: See your Google or Apple account password
See your friends list without your approval
Move progress to the other platform (iPhone to Android or back)
Sign you in when you decline or turn the service off
limits.differs: Android uses Play Games Services and signs in automatically. iPhone uses Game Center and shows a sign in prompt.

story.what_it_is: You sign into the phone's built in game account, so scores, saves and friends follow you.

marketing.name: Google Play Games services
marketing.pitch: One game profile that carries your achievements, cloud saves and leaderboards across devices.

marketing.name: Game Center
marketing.pitch: Apple's social gaming network for friends, leaderboards and achievements across your Apple devices.

story.for_you: When you open a game you see a small welcome banner with your gamer name. Your progress is saved to the account and shows up on a new phone. Friends can see your scores and invite you to play.
story.for_makers: Makers get a ready made player ID, friends list, leaderboard and cloud save without building their own. It also gives the platform a link between your play in many games, which helps with recommendations and retention.

use_cases.example: A puzzle game restores your levels and coins on a new phone after you sign in with your game account.
A racing game shows your lap time against friends on a leaderboard.
A multiplayer game uses your friends list to start a match or invite someone straight into your party.
An AR title saves your collection to the game account so a lost phone does not wipe it.
A kids game uses an account managed by a parent so achievements are saved without a new password.
A studio sees returning players across devices and counts a person once, not three phones.

story.android_note: Android uses Play Games, and it signs in automatically when the player has a Google account on the phone.
story.ios_note: iPhone uses Game Center, and the player signs in once in Settings and can turn it off per app.

history.change: Automatic sign in replaces explicit sign in
